a. Informal, Non-Hearing Procedures
Informal adjudication is a broad category of procedures (and, in some 
cases, the virtual absence of any procedures) for making decisions or 
issuing orders when an on-the-record hearing under the APA is not 
required. The APA leaves informal adjudication largely unregulated. But 
see 5 U.S.C. §§ 555 & 558. Organic statutes often contemplate final 
decisions without hearings—e.g., on initial applications or following 
investigation, inspection, examination, or other informal consultation with 
affected parties. These statutes frequently leave the procedural details to 
the agency’s discretion. The agency may fill out the details in procedural 
rules or guidance, although knowledge of the agency s customs and 
practices typically is necessary to understand the process. Informal 
adjudication is used for a vast range of decisions, from the issuance of an 
individual passport, to the designation of an organization as a foreign 
terrorist entity, to the decision to allow over-the-counter access to a 
particular drug.
